$comment: Copy this file into config/repos/ (gitignored), rename it, and edit.
Filename convention: <owner>__<repo>.json — it is only a filename, the
'repo' key below is what actually identifies the repository.
Repos are processed in filename order, so prefix with 10-, 20- etc. if you
want to control which one gets first call on your quota.
$comment_local_path: Your everyday clone. The reviewer never checks out a branch in it and
never touches refs/heads/* or refs/remotes/*. It fetches PR heads into
refs/reviewer/* and creates a detached worktree in your temp dir, which it
removes when the review finishes. Set to null to skip the worktree
entirely — reviews then run on the diff alone, with no ability to read
$comment_identity: The GitHub account the token belongs to — used to recognise our own PRs,
our own review threads, and re-review requests aimed at us.
null means: ask the token who it is, which is right almost always. Set it
to a username only if you want the check; a value that disagrees with the
token is an error rather than something the reviewer works around.
$comment_language: Language for everything a person reads: inline comments, the summary, and
replies. BCP-47 tag or plain name — 'es', 'de', 'pt-BR', 'Spanish'.
Falls back to global.default_language when omitted.
$comment_agent_language: Language for the copy-paste agent block. null means: same as 'language'.

gates.$comment: A PR is reviewed when every enabled gate passes. Set any to false to switch it off for this repo.
gates.$comment_skip_if_approved: An explicit re-review request aimed at you overrides this — you asked for it, you get it.
$comment_ignore_checks: Exact check-run names to disregard when deciding CI is green. Use for
optional or flaky checks that are not required to merge. The 'approving
review required' rule is a branch-protection setting, not a check run, so
it never appears here and never blocks the reviewer.
gates.$comment_blocking_labels: Any of these present on the PR and it is left alone. Empty list disables.
gates.$comment_required_labels: If non-empty, the PR needs at least one of these before it is reviewed.
gates.$comment_only_if_review_requested: true = review only PRs where you are a requested reviewer. false = review every PR that passes the other gates.
gates.$comment_base_branches: Restrict to PRs targeting these branches, e.g. ['main', 'develop']. Empty = any base.

$comment: Three tiers, applied in this order. Everything dropped or shortened is
listed by name in the summary comment, so a reviewed PR always says what
diff.$comment_exclude: Dropped from the diff entirely. The reviewer is told the file changed and by how many lines, and nothing else.
$comment_summarize_only: For files that occasionally matter but are usually artifacts — a
migration snapshot that adds 9,000 lines and says nothing. The reviewer
gets the path, the line counts, and the hunk headers, so it can still
say 'this migration changed, worth a human glance' without reading it.
diff.$comment_max_file_lines: A single file's patch longer than this is sent head-and-tail with an elision marker in the middle.
$comment_max_total_lines: Measured AFTER exclude and summarize_only are applied, so a PR that is
+10,000 lines of snapshot and +900 lines of real code counts as 900.
Over the limit, files are dropped lowest-risk first and the summary names
diff.$comment_context_lines: Unchanged lines kept around each hunk. Lowering to 1 or 2 cuts tokens noticeably on large diffs at some cost to readability.

$comment_axes: 'standards' — does this match the conventions in personality/ and the
repo's own documented standards? 'spec' — does it actually deliver what
the linked issue asked for? Kept separate so a clean-code pass cannot
mask a PR that builds the wrong thing. Drop 'spec' in repos where PRs
review.$comment_split: false = one call, two labelled sections (cheaper). true = one call per axis (~2x quota, stronger separation).
$comment_personality: Files from personality/, in order, concatenated into the system prompt.
These five are the general reviewer and apply to any codebase. The rest
are opt-in specialisms — add the ones this repo needs:
'30-shareability'  when something belongs in a shared package
Write your own alongside them — any personality/<name>.md can be listed
here, and a file per specialism keeps each repo's prompt to what applies.
$comment_repo_notes: Conventions specific to this repository go in a markdown file sitting next
to this one — same name, .md instead of .json. It is picked up
automatically; there is no key for it.
Prefer writing conventions in the repository itself (CLAUDE.md and friends,
read below) so they stay current for everyone. Use the notes file for what
belongs to the reviewer rather than the team.

$comment_from_ref: Where to read the target repo's own CLAUDE.md / .claude/*.md from.
'default_branch' reads code that has already been reviewed. Reading it
from the PR branch would let a PR ship instructions to its own
reviewer, which matters because this tool can approve.
A PR that modifies these files is surfaced as a finding.
repo_context.$comment_paths: .claude/skills/** is left out on purpose — those are workflow skills for building in the repo, not for reviewing it.

$comment_disagreement: Counted per thread, not per PR. Review rounds themselves are uncapped —
a PR can go fifteen rounds. What is capped is one thread ping-ponging.
At the cap that single thread goes quiet and you get a notification;
every other thread and every later round carries on.

approval.$comment_mode: 'auto' — submit reviews without asking. 'manual' — post nothing, just notify you with the drafted review saved to the state dir.
$comment_no_blocker_action: What to submit when there are findings but no blockers.
'comment_and_invite' — post the findings as COMMENT plus one line in the
summary offering to approve as-is if the author says they would rather
not take the nits. When they reply, the claim is checked the same way a
disputed thread is, and an APPROVE follows.
'approve_with_notes' — approve immediately, nits attached as comments.
'comment_only' — post findings, say nothing about approving.

manual_only_when.$comment: Conditions that force a human approval even in auto mode. Empty/null values disable a condition.
manual_only_when.$comment_touches_paths: e.g. ['**/auth/**', '**/billing/**', '**/*.sql'] to keep sensitive areas hand-approved.
